title: PixelKnot Tutorial: Hide Secret Messages Inside Images on Android 🔐
description:
🔐 Want to hide a secret message inside an ordinary picture?

In this video, we take a look at PixelKnot, an Android application designed for hiding encrypted text inside images using steganography.

PixelKnot allows you to select an image, write a secret message, protect it with a password, and embed the encrypted message into the image. The resulting picture looks like a normal image, while the hidden message can be recovered by the recipient using PixelKnot and the correct password.

🔸 What PixelKnot is

title: USB Gadget Tool on Android: Fix Rucky Kernel Not Supported Without Custom Kernel!
description:
Want to use your rooted Android phone as a USB HID device? In this video, we test USB Gadget Tool with Rucky and Kali NetHunter to enable Mouse & Keyboard HID functionality on Android.

USB Gadget Tool uses the Linux kernel's ConfigFS interface to create and activate USB gadgets. The project supports several gadget types, including Keyboard & Mouse, FIDO CTAP, CCID and UVC, provided your device has the required root access and kernel support.

In this tutorial, we configure the Mouse & Keyboard gadget, grant root permissions, enable the USB HID interfaces, and verify /dev/hidg0 and /dev/hidg1.

We then test Rucky and demonstrate the difference when the USB HID gadget is enabled versus disabled. This can be useful for rooted Android devices where you are encountering the "kernel not supported" message in Rucky.

⚠️ Requirements: • Rooted Android device • USB Gadget Tool • Kernel with ConfigFS support • Rucky or another compatible HID application • Kali NetHunter (optional for the demonstration)
